kind: descriptive, SP08 step 1 (no candidate, no gate)
item: SP08: the name-based fallback chain of TorrentStreamsService.find_by_imdb (runs only when the IMDb search yields no playable stream; queries from _build_fallback_queries run one after another, each to every tracker; the 20 s budget is checked only between queries).
question: How many fallback queries typically run before success, what does the chain cost, and could 'the first two queries concurrently, the first success cancels the rest' (the plan's candidate) save a material amount?

source.product_change_in_commit: _FALLBACK_BUDGET_SECONDS = 20.0 module constant (same value, so the harness can scale it); no behaviour change

command: cd server; HOST_IP=10.255.255.1 PYTHONPATH=. python ../scripts/benchmark_sp_fallback.py --out <file> (defaults: arm C0, matches token,token-fold,substring-fold, S1-S3, 2 rounds of 10 categories, interval 10 s, time scale 0.25, 3 trackers, 3 releases per tracker, latency 0.4 s +-25 %, slow 8 s, failure timeout, download 0.2 s, Tech Info 0.2 s, steady from request 2, seed 20261110)
environment: in-process on the developer machine (Windows, Python 3.12.10, the server venv), no Docker, run while Docker gates occupied the machine; 0.55-0.80 CPU s per (model, scenario) run.
arm: C0 = the code defaults of 06b790d: indexer_breaker_threshold 2 (120 s, doubling to 600 s), tech_info_prefetch on; durations scaled by 0.25 and reported unscaled.

materiality_rule.metric: upper-bound saving of 'first two queries concurrently' over the steady fallback cold requests, mean over the equal-weight fallback category mix (imdb-hit excluded)
materiality_rule.material_if: saving >= 1000 ms AND saving >= 20 % of the C0 mean fallback cold latency in at least one (match model, scenario) cell
materiality_rule.why: the bound is what a perfect candidate could save at most; below the rule no real candidate can be material, so step 2 stops without a candidate

materiality_rule_fixed: in scripts/benchmark_sp_fallback.py (MATERIALITY_RULE), committed in 001eaac before the measured run
outcome: NOT MATERIAL in all 9 (match model, scenario) cells -> step 2 not started: no setting, no candidate, no gate draft. SP08 closes as 'no change', as the plan expected.
analysis: Rule result: the upper bound of what a perfect 'first two concurrently' candidate saves is 183-281 ms in S1 and S2 (8.7-17.1 % of the 1.5-2.2 s mean fallback cold latency) and 1.9-4.0 s in S3 (9.4-17.7 % of 20.5-22.5 s). No cell reaches both 1 s and 20 %; the largest is token/S3 (3988 ms, 17.7 %).

Queries until success (steady fallback cold requests of the equal-weight synthetic mix): the first query finds the streams for 37.5-62.5 % (token -> substring-fold), the second for 17.6-43.8 %, the rest (18.8-25 %) is on no tracker, and no request needed a third query. A second query is needed for accented titles under accent-sensitive matching, titles whose releases drop the leading article, single-episode-only releases under token matching (the 'Title S02' query does not match 'S02E05') and absolutely numbered anime ('Title S01' never matches '- 05'). Titles on no tracker run the whole chain: 2 queries (two-word movie) or 5 (series); in S3 the 20 s budget cuts the series chain to 3 queries.

Cost of one query: p50 ~0.45-0.56 s in S1/S2 (tracker latency plus .torrent downloads of the hits); ~7.8-8.5 s in S3, because every query waits for the slow tracker although the healthy trackers answered in ~0.4 s. Query tracker calls per steady fallback request: 5.3-6.0 (S1), 3.5-3.6 (S2, subject skipped), 4.5-5.3 (S3).

At these per-query costs S1/S2 are not material for any title mix: the bound on a request that needed a second query is min(d1, d2) = 0.38-0.46 s on average, so even if every fallback request needed one it would stay below 1 s. S3 is mix-dependent: on such requests the bound is 7.2-8.0 s of 24.7-25.5 s (29-32 %); with k=1 requests at ~16 s, the mix-level bound reaches 20 % only when more than about half of the fallback requests need a second query, and only while a tracker is that slow.

S2 with the live breaker (K=2): the subject opens on the first cold request (IMDb search + first query time out), after which the chain costs what S1 does; the steady p95 of 13-13.7 s is the single probe after the 120 s cooldown (probe failed, reopened for 240 s), landing on the IMDb search or a fallback query alike. Concurrent fallback queries would not change it.

What the bound leaves out (from the code, not run): (1) every request whose first query succeeds (37.5-62.5 % here) would send one more query to every tracker, 3 -> 6 searches, plus the .torrent downloads of its hits; (2) 'the first success cancels the rest' cannot cancel that work today, because TorrentSourceProviderService.find_by_query runs in Singleflight.run, which shields the shared task (CR15/c): the tracker phase, downloads, store and Tech Info prefetch of the cancelled query run to the end unless the singleflight gets last-waiter cancellation; (3) each speculative query takes a source_search_max_parallel admission slot (12) and shares the per-indexer download gates (5) with the first query, so the k=1 path could get slower. A real candidate would save less than the bound and cost more tracker load, which is the plan's expected reason for 'no change'.

S3 is dominated by the per-query wait for the slow tracker (gather), not by the number of queries; a parallel pair would only overlap one 8 s step. That is the adaptive timeout / early partial result direction the plan deferred as SP05/c, not SP08.
caveats: Synthetic titles, releases and three tracker match models; the real trackers' matching rules and the real title mix (plan question 7, optional) are not available, so the shares above describe the synthetic mix only.

Single descriptive run, n = 16-17 steady fallback cold requests per cell (2 rounds); no repetition, no noise J. The rule's margin to the threshold (largest cell 17.7 % vs 20 %, and < 0.3 s vs 1 s in S1/S2) is the basis of the decision, not a significance test.
Time scale 0.25: product and fixture durations scale, reported unscaled; fixed in-process overhead per request is magnified 4x in latencies, but the bound is made of query durations.
imdb-hit (the other path) has n = 1-2 per cell and is descriptive only.
observations_out_of_scope: S3 warm p95 ~17 s: a chain the budget cut on the cold request (series-missing, 3 of 5 queries) continues on the warm request with the two uncached queries against the trackers.

Movie fallback acceptance rejects only a mismatching IMDb tag or a series-looking name, so a broad query (first word of the title) could accept untagged releases of another movie; the harness uses unique words and cannot show this. Not measured, not changed.
